userdoc.notice: Points reserved names of a registry at one resolver, each name in a single call. A reserved name has no owner and so no roles, and a registry lets no account set resolvers registry-wide, so a reservation's resolver cannot be changed in place. This contract moves it instead, in one transaction: it registers the reservation to itself with only the role to unregister it, unregisters it, and reserves it again with the resolver, the same subregistry and the same expiry. The name is never left unreserved between transactions, and unregistering bumps its resource, so the role taken in the first step does not outlive the call. It needs the registry's root `ROLE_REGISTRAR` and `ROLE_REGISTER_RESERVED` while it works, and only its owner can call it. Once those roles are revoked it can do nothing.
